A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BREW watermarking study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are available and readable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermark detection, text-quality, robustness, runtime, and payload-recovery experiments in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, including results on C4 and OpenGen, with limited numerical revisions.

M1.justification: Block-wise embedding, blind message estimation, designated verification, and shared global-offset search are retained. Algorithm 3's revised branching is equivalent: both versions select the nonzero codeword when its paired candidate is zero. Explicit generation length and mask descriptions clarify the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate C4 and OpenGen under clean conditions, token-preserving, token-reducing, and token-increasing synonym substitution, and T5-based paraphrasing. Renamed attack captions describe the same scenarios.

E2.justification: MPAC and Qu et al. (2025) remain the evaluated external comparators. RBC is explicitly excluded in both versions. The appendix comparisons retain the same naive detector, embedding variants, and ablation variants.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 revises its stated BCH configurations from (31,16,3), (63,45,3), and (127,92,5) to (15,5,3), (31,6,7), and (63,7,15), aligning that description with configurations already evaluated in v1's Section 5.2. This changes reported settings but does not establish reruns; the main evaluation protocols, metrics, and parameter sweeps remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the designated-verification/window-shifting ablation, shift-range and embedding-strength sensitivities, codeword comparisons, threshold analysis, BER analysis, and payload-recovery evaluation. No new robustness experiment or supplementary empirical analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Both use the same point-estimate reporting practice. Neither adds repeated-run counts, experimental seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 5 changes Qu et al.'s BLEU/BERTScore at delta=2 from 22.31/0.7740 to 26.44/0.7996. In Table 22, BREW on OpenGen with OPT-1.3B, 10% token-increasing substitution, T=200, delta=6, and smax=3 changes FPR/precision/F1 from 0.0400/0.8750/0.4240 to 0.0650/0.9161/0.8000; TPR remains 0.7100. These are isolated revisions under unchanged stated conditions; the remaining experimental results and plotted curves are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix C.4 adds a formal inequality relating global-offset detection to per-block maximization. Theorem C.5 permits independent Bernoulli variables with probabilities bounded by p, replacing identical Bernoulli(p) variables. Theorem C.3 explicitly qualifies its idealized uniform null model, Remark C.7 corrects doubly-exponential to exponential suppression, and Example 1 updates its shift-budget calculation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same verification-centric method, reliability claims, model-agnostic scope, and headline TPR/FPR result. Prioritizing reliable short payloads over maximum capacity was already stated in v1's conclusion.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 replaces language about handling local desynchronization with a bounded-global-desynchronization qualification. New Appendix B.3 expands and quantifies the claimed capacity–reliability trade-off. Appendix D.3 corrects the interpretation of unchanged perplexities: BREW's 24.46 is higher, rather than lower, than MPAC's 24.09.

D1.justification: Section 3.1.1 explicitly explains that the block mask is deterministically derived from the key and block index, and Algorithm 1 specifies generation length T. Appendix B.2.3 replaces the recommendation of smax=10 with an explanation of the experimental default smax=5, already reported in v1's main text.

R1.justification: The cited works and extraction-versus-verification positioning remain the same. The additional capacity paragraph develops the existing short-payload positioning. Reference revisions concern bibliographic metadata rather than added literature.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted explanatory rewrites in Sections 3.3, C.3–C.4, and D.3, adds Appendix B.3, and renumbers subsequent B subsections. Terminology, grammar, affiliations, publication information, and acknowledgments receive local edits; the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: All 11 figures and 23 tables are retained, with unchanged figure contents. Figures, tables, and algorithms shift within the layout, including Figure 3 moving from page 8 to page 9. Captions standardize attack terminology, and Table 7 standardizes smax notation; the displays are not substantially redesigned.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reporting consistency through Table 22's corrected metrics, Appendix D.3's corrected perplexity comparison, and Appendix B.1's alignment with the existing experiments. The explicit inequality in C.4 and bounded-global-shift qualification make the theoretical scope clearer. These are useful local improvements, although the theoretical cleanup remains incomplete: Corollary C.8 still retains the doubly-exponential wording corrected in Remark C.7.
